g.passage: Lakeside, my thirtieth summer, kept its promenade swept for visitors who were not us. Each evening I carried Mother's folding stool along the boards, opened it at the rail, and stood behind her while she watched the lake for the Buffalo steamer that had once brought my brother Cyrus home. Cyrus had gone east to read law on the money Father left; I had stayed, and the stool had come with staying. I learned to open it one-handed. In August a letter came saying that Cyrus would not visit that year either. Mother read it twice, folded it into her sleeve, and asked for nothing. That evening I set the stool down as usual, but my hand stayed a long while on the canvas seat, pressing where it sagged. At the end of the boards, when Mother rose to walk the last stretch on her cane, I did not fold it. I sat down upon it and watched the water myself, and she, after a moment, came back and stood beside me.

Each afternoon Zofia carried a chair out, set it beside the fountain, and sat facing the landlord's window with her shawl crossed tight. Her patience was a dry basin waiting for the thaw. Sipho watched his grandmother arrange the tomatoes in a single row, then a pyramid, then a row again, pressing each with her thumb before setting it down. Aster lifted a cloth from a basket under the table. Inside were six yellow tomatoes, each wrapped in newspaper, each with a penciled name: the regulars who had bought them every week before the drought. She found the woman's name and handed the parcel over without taking money. Sipho looked at the five still in the basket. Aster slid it back under the table and returned to pressing the red ones, one by one, while the crowd moved past.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It begins with a sparse table, then details Aster's repeated arranging, and ends with crowds passing.
It begins with a customer's request, then gives Sipho's assumption, and ends with Aster's routine resumed.
It begins with a sparse table, then shows a customer's request, and ends with every regular provided for.
It begins with Sipho reading a gesture, then shows a request revising it, and ends with parcels waiting.
g.explanation: 지문은 Sipho가 할머니의 토마토 정리 동작을 수확 부족을 감추는 행동으로 읽는 관찰로 시작한다. 이어 손님의 요청으로 단골 이름이 적힌 노란 토마토 바구니가 드러나면서, 그 동작이 단골을 챙기는 마음일 수 있다는 재해석이 일어난다. 마지막에는 아직 바구니에 남은 다섯 꾸러미와 다시 이어지는 동작으로 장면이 해결되지 않은 채 끝나므로 D가 정답이다. A는 전반부만 요약했고, B는 관찰과 요청의 순서를 뒤집었으며, C는 결말을 모든 단골이 챙겨진 해결로 오독했다.

seed.topicSeed: a clock-maker's shop in Havana; a landlord's son and a tenant's daughter over silence kept to protect someone

g.passage: Why did Hedwig wind the clocks backward? Kalani, the landlord's son, had noticed it on three rent days running: while her father counted coins at the bench of the little Havana shop, she moved along the wall of clocks and turned each key the wrong way, gently, until it resisted, and then let it go. He took it for a girl's idle mischief and said nothing, since his own father disliked complaints. On the fourth rent day his father asked to see the shop's account book. Hedwig's father went pale and reached for the drawer, but Hedwig was quicker; she set the book on the counter herself, opened to a page in her own neat hand, and stepped back to the clocks. Kalani, reading over his father's shoulder, saw that every entry was dated a week before the coins had truly come in. His father nodded and closed the book. Hedwig turned one more key the wrong way and looked at Kalani, and he held her gaze without a word.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It begins with a puzzling habit observed, then shows a request recasting it, and ends with a choice pending.
It begins with Kalani suspecting fraud, then shows the habit as mischief, and ends with a choice still pending.
It begins with a puzzling habit observed, then describes rent being counted, and ends with coins on the bench.
It begins with a puzzling habit observed, then shows a request that recasts it, and ends with the debt resolved.
g.explanation: 지문은 Hedwig가 시계 태엽을 거꾸로 감는 습관을 Kalani가 장난으로 여기는 관찰로 시작한다. 이어 장부를 보자는 요청이 나오고, 그녀가 직접 써 둔 날짜가 실제보다 한 주 앞당겨져 있다는 사실이 드러나며 그 동작이 시간을 되돌려 아버지를 감싸는 행동으로 다시 읽힌다. 마지막에 Hedwig가 Kalani를 바라보고 그가 말없이 시선을 받는 장면은 그가 침묵할지 결정되지 않은 채 끝나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 인식의 순서를 뒤집었고, C는 전반부만 요약했으며, D는 열린 결말을 빚 문제의 해결로 오독했다.
